findings.title: Numeric discrete labels passed to hue= are colored as continuous values on a CYCLIC hls palette -- extreme labels get identical colors; shipped plot_clusters2 gallery figure is effectively monochrome
findings.description: plot.py:2014 classifies ANY 1-D numeric hue as continuous (hue_is_continuous), and the continuous path maps values onto seaborn 'hls' -- a CLOSED hue circle where the first and last of the 100 bins are the same red (hls(100)[0]=(0.86,0.3712,0.34), hls(100)[99]=(0.86,0.34,0.34)). Consequences: (a) binary int cluster labels (exactly what examples/plot_clusters2.py teaches: hue=hyp.cluster(data, n_clusters=2)) render as two indistinguishable reds -- the shipped gallery figure shows one apparent color, defeating the example's stated purpose 'color our points by cluster'; (b) k=3 int labels give clusters 0 and 2 the SAME red (verify_hue_int_k3.png shows two red blobs + one cyan -- a scientist would misread cluster membership); (c) identical labels as strings take the categorical path and get properly distinct colors (str/int inconsistency); (d) legend=True is refused for int labels ('legend is not supported for continuous or matrix-valued hue') even though they are discrete; (e) for genuinely continuous hue the wrap-around means min and max values are always the same color, and continuous_colormap() colorbars have identical ends. Fix directions: treat small-cardinality integer hue as categorical (like str), and/or use a non-cyclic palette for the continuous path.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
np.random.seed(0)
c1 = np.random.multivariate_normal(np.zeros(3), np.eye(3), size=100)
c2 = np.random.multivariate_normal(np.zeros(3)+3, np.eye(3), size=100)
data = np.vstack([c1, c2])
labels = hyp.cluster(data, n_clusters=2)
fig = hyp.plot(data, '.', hue=labels, show=False)
cols = {tuple(np.round(np.asarray(c)[:3],3)) for coll in fig.axes[0].collections for c in coll.get_facecolor()}
print(cols)  # {(0.86,0.34,0.34),(0.86,0.371,0.34)} -- visually identical reds
findings.expected: Two clearly distinct colors for the two clusters (hls(2) = red (0.86,0.371,0.34) and cyan (0.34,0.829,0.86), as produced when the same labels are passed as strings), and a legend available for discrete labels.
findings.actual: distinct point colors in hue=cluster_labels plot: 2 [(0.86, 0.34, 0.34), (0.86, 0.371, 0.34)]  |  k=3 int hue: [(0.34,0.829,0.86),(0.86,0.34,0.34),(0.86,0.371,0.34)] (clusters 0 and 2 both red)  |  hls(100)[0]=(0.86,0.3712,0.34), hls(100)[99]=(0.86,0.34,0.34)  |  WARN UserWarning: legend is not supported for continuous or matrix-valued hue; ignoring legend.

findings.title: plot_autoencoders gallery figure: VariationalAutoencoder panel is a degenerate collapsed embedding (deterministically, every docs build)
findings.description: The third panel of examples/plot_autoencoders.py (VariationalAutoencoder, epochs=30, batch_size=32, random_state=0) collapses to a near-vertical line spanning ~0.03x0.07 coordinate units (PCA panel spans 47.9x26.3) with thoroughly mixed manifold colors (|spearman| of embedding dims vs manifold parameter t: 0.225/0.388 -- i.e. the embedding does not track the manifold). Because random_state=0 makes it deterministic, the SHIPPED docs figure will always show this degenerate panel, directly under prose claiming autoencoders 'can unfold nonlinear structure that PCA (linear) cannot'. The example needs different VAE hyperparameters (more epochs, KL warm-up/lower beta, different architecture) or should drop the VAE panel; as-is the gallery demonstrates the feature failing.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
t = np.linspace(0, 3*np.pi, 300)
manifold = np.column_stack([t*np.cos(t), t*np.sin(t)])
data = manifold @ rng.standard_normal((2,10)) + 0.05*rng.standard_normal((300,10))
kw = {'epochs':30,'batch_size':32,'random_state':0}
v = np.asarray(hyp.reduce(data, reduce={'model':'VariationalAutoencoder','kwargs':kw}, ndims=2))
print(np.ptp(v[:,0]), np.ptp(v[:,1]))  # ~0.0343 0.0669
findings.expected: A VAE panel showing the manifold unfolded (or at least structured), with span comparable to the data scale, supporting the example's pedagogical claim.
findings.actual: VAE deterministic across runs: True; VAE span x: 0.0343 y: 0.0669; PCA span x: 47.9 y: 26.3; VAE dim-vs-t |spearman|: 0.225, 0.388 (panel renders as a collapsed line with mixed colors)

findings.title: plot_align.py silently drops subject 18 of 36 (index 17) when averaging into two groups
findings.description: hyp.load('weights') returns 36 datasets. The example averages group1 = np.mean(data[:17], 0) (indices 0-16, 17 subjects) and group2 = np.mean(data[18:], 0) (indices 18-35, 18 subjects) -- index 17 belongs to neither group, so one subject's data is silently discarded and the groups are unequal (17 vs 18). The prose says 'we average the data into two groups', which a reader will take as an 18/18 split. Should be data[:18] / data[18:].
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
data = hyp.load('weights')
print(len(data), len(data[:17]), len(data[18:]))  # 36 17 18 -> index 17 dropped
findings.expected: All 36 subjects partitioned into two groups (data[:18] and data[18:]).
findings.actual: type: list len: 36; group1 idx 0..16 (17), group2 idx 18..35 (18), dropped: [17]

findings.title: plot_pipelines_return_model.py multi-stage demo aligns a 200-row train set with an 80-row test set, silently trimming 120 train rows (with warning)
findings.description: The multi-stage return_model section runs hyp.reduce([train, test], ..., align='HyperAlign', ...) on datasets of 200 and 80 rows. Alignment trims both to the 80 common rows, emitting 'UserWarning: alignment keeps only the 80 row(s) common to all datasets; datasets with more rows were trimmed.' The example never prints multi_out shapes, so a reader following this canonical train/test pattern loses 60% of the training data without the prose acknowledging it. The example should use equal-length datasets for the align stage or explain the trimming.
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python examples/plot_pipelines_return_model.py  # observe UserWarning about trimming to 80 rows
findings.expected: Multi-stage demo where no data is discarded (equal-length datasets), or prose explaining that alignment requires matching row counts.
findings.actual: === WARN UserWarning: alignment keeps only the 80 row(s) common to all datasets; datasets with more rows were trimmed. Align datasets with matching numbers of observations to avoid d[ata loss...]

findings.title: plot_mixture_models.py 'equivalently' claim: the two figures use permuted component colors because GaussianMixture is refit unseeded
findings.description: The example prints proportions from one hyp.cluster call, then (fig1) lets hyp.plot(cluster='GaussianMixture') REFIT internally and (fig2) plots hue=proportions from the first fit. hyp.cluster('GaussianMixture') sets no random_state, so identical calls return permuted component orders (verified: argmax head [1 1 1 1 1] vs [2 2 2 2 2]) -- the two 'equivalent' figures show the same blobs in permuted/reversed colors (observed red->blue->green vs green->blue->red), and gallery figures change across builds. Passing a seed and/or reusing the printed proportions for fig1 would make the demo actually equivalent.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100,5)) + 1.5*i for i in range(3)])
p1 = np.asarray(hyp.cluster(data, cluster='GaussianMixture', n_clusters=3))
p2 = np.asarray(hyp.cluster(data, cluster='GaussianMixture', n_clusters=3))
print(np.array_equal(p1.argmax(1), p2.argmax(1)))  # False
findings.expected: The two plots render with identical color-to-component assignment, matching the prose 'equivalently, pass any (n_samples, k) matrix as hue'.
findings.actual: same argmax component ids across two identical calls: False; argmax head p1: [1 1 1 1 1] p2: [2 2 2 2 2]; fig1 colors left-to-right red/blue/green, fig2 green/blue/red

findings.title: hyp.reduce silently returns the input unchanged when ndims >= n_features, even for explicitly requested nonlinear embeddings (TSNE)
findings.description: hyp.reduce(data30x5, reduce='TSNE', ndims=50) raises no error and returns the RAW input array untouched (allclose to input: True). No warning is emitted. A user who requests a TSNE embedding gets back their original data with no indication that no embedding was computed. Skipping is a defensible convention for linear reducers, but doing it silently -- and for nonlinear embeddings where k-D TSNE output is not the same thing as k-D raw data -- can produce wrong downstream science. At minimum a warning should be emitted.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
data = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((30,5))
out = np.asarray(hyp.reduce(data, reduce='TSNE', ndims=50))
print(out.shape, np.allclose(out, data))  # (30, 5) True -- silent passthrough
findings.expected: Either an error (sklearn TSNE itself rejects n_components>3 with barnes_hut) or a loud warning that reduction was skipped because ndims >= n_features.
findings.actual: TSNE ndims=50 -> (30, 5); passthrough (allclose to input): True; no warning captured

findings.title: normalize='bogus' fails with AssertionError naming the internal parameter 'scale_type' instead of a ValueError naming the user-facing kwarg
findings.description: hyp.plot(data, normalize='bogus') (and hyp.normalize) raises 'AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.' The message content is helpful (lists valid values) but: (a) AssertionError is the wrong exception type for input validation and disappears entirely under python -O, silently accepting the bad value; (b) 'scale_type' is an internal name -- the user passed normalize=. Compare the excellent messages from cluster/align dispatchers ('unknown cluster model ...; supported names: ...' as ValueError).
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.plot(np.random.rand(30,5), normalize='bogus', show=False)"
findings.expected: ValueError: normalize must be one of 'across', 'within', 'row', None, or a fitted Normalizer (got 'bogus').
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: Autoencoder reducers silently accept invalid training hyperparameters (epochs=-5 returns an untrained embedding)
findings.description: hyp.reduce(data, reduce={'model':'Autoencoder','kwargs':{'epochs':-5}}, ndims=2) runs without error or warning and returns a finite (30,2) array from an encoder that trained for zero passes. A typo'd hyperparameter thus yields garbage embeddings that look plausible. epochs (and batch_size etc.) should be validated as positive integers.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
data = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((30,5))
out = hyp.reduce(data, reduce={'model':'Autoencoder','kwargs':{'epochs':-5}}, ndims=2)
print(np.asarray(out).shape)  # (30, 2), no error/warning
findings.expected: ValueError: epochs must be a positive integer (got -5).
findings.actual: NO ERROR; AE epochs=-5 -> (30, 2) finite: True

findings.title: import hypertools.<subpackage>.<module> as <name> fails with a cryptic ImportError once hypertools is imported (function shadowing of subpackage names)
findings.description: hypertools/__init__.py rebinds subpackage names (reduce, cluster, align, ...) to their same-named FUNCTIONS. The 'import X.Y.Z as m' form resolves Z via getattr on the parent attribute chain, hits the function instead of the subpackage, and dies with "ImportError: cannot import name 'describe' from 'reduce' (unknown location)". The same statement WITHOUT 'as' works (sys.modules path), as does 'from hypertools.align.procrustes import procrustes' (used by plot_procrustes.py). Power users following the gallery's submodule-import pattern with an 'as' alias get an unexplainable error.
findings.repro: .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; import hypertools.reduce.describe as dmod"
findings.expected: Import succeeds (as it does without the 'as' alias), or documentation warns that subpackage attribute names are shadowed by functions.
findings.actual: ImportError: cannot import name 'describe' from 'reduce' (unknown location)

findings.title: describe(): show=True default calls plt.show() (UserWarning headless); show=False leaves NO way to get the figure; figure has 4 same-color unlabeled curves
findings.description: hyp.describe(data) (as in examples/plot_describe.py) internally calls plt.show(), emitting 'UserWarning: FigureCanvasAgg is non-interactive, and thus cannot be shown' in every headless run including the docs build. With show=False the function returns only the dict {'average','individual'} and no figure exists afterward (plt.get_fignums() == []), so there is no programmatic way to obtain/save the plot. The figure itself draws the 3 individual-dataset curves and the average curve in the SAME color with no legend, so they cannot be told apart (example prose says it 'plots their correlation' without saying what each line is).
findings.repro:
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp
res = hyp.describe(hyp.load('weights_sample'), show=False)
print(sorted(res.keys()), plt.get_fignums())  # ['average','individual'] []
findings.expected: describe(show=False) returns or retains the figure (e.g. a 'fig' entry in the dict); curves distinguished by color/legend (individual vs average); no forced plt.show() side effect in library code.
findings.actual: describe returns: dict ['average', 'individual']; figs open after describe(show=False): []; runner warning: '=== WARN UserWarning: FigureCanvasAgg is non-interactive, and thus cannot be shown'; saved figure shows overlapping same-color unlabeled curves

findings.title: Unseeded RNG in plot_normalize/plot_clusters2/plot_PPCA (and unseeded GaussianMixture in plot_mixture_models) makes gallery figures irreproducible; PPCA example's actual missing fraction is ~9.3%, not 10%
findings.description: plot_normalize.py, plot_clusters2.py and plot_PPCA.py draw np.random.* data without a seed, so every docs build renders different figures (the newer examples plot_apply_model/plot_pipelines_return_model/plot_autoencoders/plot_mixture_models all correctly use default_rng(seed) for data). Additionally plot_PPCA.py selects missing entries via np.random.choice(len(inds), len(inds)*0.1) WITH replacement, so only ~9.3% unique entries are actually removed despite 'missing = .1'.

findings.expected: Seeded examples (reproducible docs figures); replace=False sampling so exactly 10% of entries are removed.

findings.title: Unused imports and a spelling error in four gallery examples
findings.description: plot_procrustes.py imports numpy and scipy but uses neither (and its prose misspells 'procustes function'); plot_normalize.py imports matplotlib.pyplot unused; plot_clusters2.py imports scipy.stats.multivariate_normal unused (data uses np.random.multivariate_normal); plot_clusters3.py imports pandas unused. Copy-paste-ready gallery code should be clean.
findings.expected: Only used imports; 'procrustes' spelled correctly in prose.
findings.actual: plot_procrustes.py:18-19 'import numpy as np / import scipy' (unused), prose line 8: 'the procustes function'; plot_normalize.py:24 'import matplotlib.pyplot as plt' (unused); plot_clusters2.py:18 'from scipy.stats import multivariate_normal' (unused); plot_clusters3.py:19 'import pandas as pd' (unused)

findings.title: plot_PPCA.py emits a matplotlib 'linestyle is redundantly defined' UserWarning (hyp.plot passes both a fmt string and the linestyle kwarg)
findings.description: hyp.plot([data1, data2], linestyle=['-',':'], ...) internally also passes a fmt string, producing 'UserWarning: linestyle is redundantly defined by the ''linestyle'' keyword argument and the fmt string "-" (-> linestyle=''-''). The keyword argument will take precedence.' The plot is correct (kwarg wins) but the warning appears in the gallery output for a documented usage pattern; hyp.plot should not forward a conflicting fmt when an explicit linestyle kwarg is given.
findings.expected: No warning for the documented linestyle=[...] usage.
findings.actual: === WARN UserWarning: linestyle is redundantly defined by the 'linestyle' keyword argument and the fmt string "-" (-> linestyle='-'). The keyword argument will take precedence.

findings.title: plot_clusters / plot_clusters3 render unordered mushroom rows as connected LINES (scribble blobs); HDBSCAN noise label -1 is colored like an ordinary cluster
findings.description: Both examples omit a marker fmt, so hypertools' default line style connects consecutive rows of the dummy-coded mushrooms table within each cluster -- producing meaningless scribble patches for data with no row ordering (see evidence). Passing '.' or 'o' would give honest point clouds. Additionally the HDBSCAN run yields 20 clusters plus 32 noise points labeled -1, and the noise group is assigned a normal palette color, indistinguishable from a real cluster (conventionally noise is gray/muted); the example prose never mentions noise.
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python examples/plot_clusters.py  # and plot_clusters3.py; labels: hyp.cluster(hyp.load('mushrooms'), cluster={'model':'HDBSCAN','params':{'min_samples':5,'min_cluster_size':30}})
findings.expected: Point markers for unordered tabular data; HDBSCAN noise visually de-emphasized or at least mentioned in prose.

findings.title: plot_TSNE / plot_UMAP class-colored figures have no legend although legend=True works for string hue
findings.description: Both digits examples color points by class label strings ('0'-'5') but the figures give no way to map colors to digits. legend=True with a categorical string hue works and shows the category names (verified: labels ['0','1','2','3','4','5']); adding it to both examples would make the gallery figures self-explanatory.
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp; from sklearn import datasets
d = datasets.load_digits(n_class=6)
hyp.plot(d.data, '.', reduce='TSNE', hue=d.target.astype('str'), ndims=2, legend=True, show=False)
findings.expected: Gallery figures with a class legend.
findings.actual: legend present: False (both shipped examples); with legend=True: legend exists: True labels: ['0', '1', '2', '3', '4', '5']

findings.title: DataFrame path (mushrooms examples) triggers Pandas4Warning from df2mat's select_dtypes(include=['object']) -- will break on a future pandas
findings.description: Running plot_clusters.py / plot_clusters3.py emits 'Pandas4Warning: For backward compatibility, ''str'' dtypes are included by select_dtypes when ''object'' dtype is specified. This behavior is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.' Source: hypertools/tools/df2mat.py:32-33 (select_dtypes(include=['object']) / exclude=['object']). When pandas removes the compatibility behavior, string columns of DataFrames (the entire mushrooms example) will silently stop being dummy-coded. Should select str dtypes explicitly.
findings.expected: No deprecation warning; dtype selection robust to pandas 4 ('str' selected explicitly).
findings.actual: === WARN Pandas4Warning: For backward compatibility, 'str' dtypes are included by select_dtypes when 'object' dtype is specified. This behavior is deprecated and will be removed in a fu[ture version]
